title: Admission annotations and onboarding readiness for unpinned open-model variants
creator: Ravi Patel
description: PRD-lite: define minimal admission annotations, runtime guarantees, and staged acceptance steps for open-source model variants that we do NOT pin by default. Goal: let platform teams onboard experimental community weights with explicit compatibility metadata and safety gates so hosted/Dedicated/Private customers can opt in without surprising regressions. This ticket clarifies scope (annotations + intake checks + failover semantics), not the full UI or ingestion pipeline automation. It captures required metadata fields, sanity test harness expectations, and a rollback/mitigation checklist for when runtime incompatibilities surface.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Annotation schema defined and documented with field-level descriptions (format: JSON lines) including: runtime_compat_level, known_incompatible_ops, recommended_quant_profiles, max_seq_len_tested, kv_cache_behavior_hint, and sample_inputs_hash

A2: Onboarding checklist that can be completed by PM/Eng/Integrator: metadata present, sanity-compiled run on target runtime (smoke-run outputs), basic eval on 3 prompt families, and explicit pinning recommendation (pin_required | soft_pin | unpinned_with_notes)

A3: Failover semantics specified: if runtime loader fails or latency spikes occur, route policy must fallback to a compatible pinned variant or return a clear error payload with recommended alternative model and reason_code

A4: A minimal set of automated sanity checks implemented in the ingest pipeline (binary size, tokenizer alignment, kv-cache shape test, and a deterministic forward pass smoke test) and their pass/fail thresholds documented
A5: Acceptance playbook includes upgrade and deprecation steps: how to notify customers, how to roll forward a pin, and how to mark variant as deprecated in the catalog UI/metadata
A6: Product, Eng, and Security have reviewed and signed off on the schema doc and the risk mitigation checklist (document PR + one follow-up comments review cycle)
A7: Example of two community model entries (one soft-pinned, one unpinned-with-notes) added to staging catalog for runtime-team verification
